newsitem.title: UK: Co-operation seen key to insurance bonds - broker.
newsitem.headline: Co-operation seen key to insurance bonds - broker.

text.p: Interest in developing capital market products for trading insurance risks remains strong, but until interested parties work together they are unlikely to take off in a big way, Willis Faber & Dumas Limited said in its latest Market Review.
"As ever the key to success will lie in co-operation between parties with the different skill sets and there are growing signs of progress in this area," the Willis Corroon Group Plc subsidiary said.
Educating capital market investors on the risk characteristics of these new products is proving harder than was realised and no one organisation has all the answers.

Willis Faber believes investment banks, securities companies, insurers and reinsurers will need to pool their expertise. It adds that there is no question of a shortage of interest in capital market products.

"There are very few major buyers of reinsurance and insurance who are not actively watching the whole area of capital markets and trying to assess when the products and markets will be sufficiently well developed to satisfy their requirements."

Some organisations are prepared to invest in deals simply to increase "their knowledge base and credibility without any real concern over the cost or the risk that public failure posed to their reputations."
Despite the high level of interest and willingness to experiment, very few deals have so far been successfully completed, Willis Faber notes.
The Chicago Board of Trade Property Claims Service (PCS) is the one exception and is likely to be followed by California Earthquake Authority with its catastrophe bonds.
